## Pull request overview

This PR fixes a cold-start persistence gap in `ObjectQLPlugin` by restoring previously saved metadata from the `sys_metadata` table during kernel boot, so user-created objects/views/apps survive redeployments.

**Changes:**
- Added a startup hydration step in `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` that calls `protocol.loadMetaFromDb()` after driver init and before schema sync.
- Introduced integration tests covering successful restore, graceful failure, and restore-before-schema-sync ordering.
- Added a changelog entry under `[Unreleased] > Fixed`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts | Adds `restoreMetadataFromDb()` and invokes it during `start()` to hydrate the in-memory registry from DB before schema sync. |
| packages/objectql/src/plugin.integration.test.ts | Adds integration tests validating metadata restoration behavior and ordering. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Documents the cold-start metadata restoration fix. |

`restoreMetadataFromDb` relies on `ctx.getService('protocol') as any` to access `loadMetaFromDb`, but `loadMetaFromDb` is not part of the typed protocol contract (and the `as any` defeats type-safety). Consider introducing a local `ProtocolWithDbRestore` type + type guard (or extending the protocol contract with an optional `loadMetaFromDb?`) so this call is type-checked and discoverable.

The catch-all log message `DB metadata restore skipped (non-fatal)` can be misleading because this `try` also covers non-DB failures (e.g., `getService('protocol')` throwing, permission enforcement, async-service error). Consider narrowing the try/catch (separate service resolution from DB hydration) or adjusting the message/fields (e.g., include a structured error object/stack) so operators can distinguish missing protocol vs DB/table issues.

This test persists an app record with `type: 'app'`, but the registry’s canonical app helpers/validation are keyed under `'apps'` (e.g., `SchemaRegistry.registerApp()` stores type `'apps'`). Using `'apps'` here would better reflect how apps are typically registered/persisted and would catch type-normalization issues earlier.

The assertion checks `registry.getItem('app', ...)`, which may not match how the rest of the code consumes apps (often via `getAllApps()` / `'apps'` type). Consider asserting against the canonical app storage (`'apps'` / `getAllApps()`) so the test validates end-to-end behavior rather than a type alias that might not be used by consumers.

```suggestion
      expect(registry.getAllApps()).toContainEqual({
```
